note: Stage 0 golden numbers for THREEJS-MIGRATION.md section 5.0. Captured on the pre-migration build at commit 5ef4be8, cache key v=95.
gpu: ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU, D3D11)
stills: base_b_inside_soil.png  (eye forced inside the box, in chamber air: tank must still render - B10)

determinism.finding: The renderer is NOT frame-deterministic with depth of field enabled. Three consecutive G.render() calls on a frozen scene differ from each other by 2700-5300 pixels, max channel-sum 10-12, out of 960000.
determinism.isolatedBy: Turning each post effect off in turn. fx.ao/bloom/rays off still differ; fx.dof=0 alone gives 0 differing pixels.
determinism.consequence: THREEJS-MIGRATION.md section 5 asks for pixel A/B against previous-stage stills, and Stage 1 for bit-identical. That is unachievable as written unless DOF is off.
determinism.recipe: Set Game.fxSettings.dof = 0 before every comparison capture and restore afterwards. With DOF off the frame is bit-exact and A/B is meaningful.
determinism.note: This is also a live bug in its own right: a paused game shimmers. Not fixed here - out of scope for the migration - but worth an entry in BUGS.md.

stage1.what: three.js r180 adopted on the existing canvas and context; renders nothing.
stage1.whyR180: r169 has no THREE.ExternalTexture, which the brief's Stage 2 needs to let a three material sample the still-raw sceneFB. It lands in r180.
stage1.verification: Same JS task, identical frozen scene, dof off, R.three present vs null: 0 differing pixels of 960000.

resetStateWritesGlState.finding: three.resetState() in r180 does not only reset three's CACHE, it writes GL state to three's defaults. Measured at frameStart: depthMask false->true, blend dst ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA->ZERO, current program->null, clearColor (0,0,0,1)->(0,0,0,0).
resetStateWritesGlState.impact: With three merely adopted and drawing nothing, the frame changed by 222547 pixels of 960000. Pinning the clear colour around resetState brought it to exactly 0.
resetStateWritesGlState.cause: The renderer sets a clear colour before the scene clear but inherits the ambient one elsewhere, so it had always relied on nobody else touching it.
resetStateWritesGlState.fix: renderer.js threeResync() wraps resetState and restores gl.clearColor(0,0,0,1). One place, so a later stage cannot reintroduce it by adding a resetState call.
resetStateWritesGlState.briefGap: THREEJS-MIGRATION.md L14 warns that raw GL desyncs three's cache. The reverse - resetState moving real GL state under the hand-written passes - is not mentioned and is what actually bit.

statsCaveat: H.stats() draws/instances/tris scale with how much colony there is, not with the renderer. They ran 38/666/92556 at 4000 frames and 44/714/129646 at 5500. Compare them only at the same simulation age; the bit-identical pixel A/B is the real gate.

vendoring.note: r17x+ splits the browser build into three.core.min.js plus three.module.min.js, which imports from core AND re-exports it with an export{...}from"..." statement. Both forms have to be handled or the wrapper does not parse.

stage3.what: sceneFB, copyFB, compFB, the AO pair and the shadow target are three WebGLRenderTargets, behind an adapter that presents the GLX.FBO surface.
stage3.sceneTarget: MRT count 2 (RGBA16F + RGBA8) with a FloatType DepthTexture, compareFunction null. Verified COMPLETE with both colour attachments and depth reported as TEXTURE.
stage3.shadowTarget: depth-only: 0 entries in .color, drawBuffers([NONE]) asserted on every bind, LINEAR depth guarded on OES_texture_float_linear.

rebuildIsNotAB.finding: Reallocating render targets and comparing stills does not work as a stage gate. Rebuilding to the SAME backend twice differs by ~43,000 pixels, which is indistinguishable from three-vs-glx (~42,000) and glx-vs-glx (~44,000).
rebuildIsNotAB.cause: The first measurement after any target rebuild is unsettled - R.resize also rebuilds the water module's targets, and its ping-pong buffers need a few frames. Not the never-cleared shadow map: clearing it by hand changed nothing.
rebuildIsNotAB.recipe: Discard the first reading after a resize or a scene change and let ~10 frames pass. With that, the water halo metric is reproducible to +/-20 px.
rebuildIsNotAB.briefGap: Section 5 asks for a pixel A/B against the previous stage's stills, but Stage 3 by definition reallocates ~26 targets, so that comparison can only ever read its own settling noise. Use the functional gates instead.

stage4.what: The entire post chain draws through three: SSAO + bilateral blur, the bloom pyramid, CoC/DoF, god rays, the composite and the FXAA blit to the default framebuffer.

gates.farPlaneSentinel: 0 pixels near 0.5, 226405 at the far plane, depth range 0.9805-0.9992. B23 intact.
gates.inkOutline: 3276 px darkened, 0.34% of the frame - present on edges, absent from flat ground and sky.
gates.lowPreset: ao/dof/rays/bloom all off: 99.9% of the frame lit, no black screen.

resyncBeforeNotJustAfter.finding: L14 says resetState after every raw GL block. In a frame that alternates raw and three passes - every frame for the whole migration - it is also needed BEFORE every three pass.
resyncBeforeNotJustAfter.symptom: Does not look like a state bug. A raw fbo.bind() sets gl.viewport behind three's back; three's cache still holds the old value, decides its own viewport call is redundant on the next setRenderTarget, and the pass draws into a stale rectangle.
resyncBeforeNotJustAfter.measured: With god rays skipped, raysFB2.bind() left the viewport at 300x200 and the composite wrote a 300x200 corner of a 1200x800 target - 93.7% of the frame pure black - while sceneFB itself was perfectly full at 1200x800. Localised by reading the bounding box of lit pixels in each target in turn.
resyncBeforeNotJustAfter.fix: T3 Pass.render resyncs on entry as well as exit.

stage5_group1_props.what: The seven prop batches draw through three: InstancedBufferGeometry wrapping the SAME five Float32Arrays push() already writes, so no call site changed.
stage5_group1_props.abVsRawPath: 1 differing pixel out of 921,600, max channel delta 11 - the three path reproduces the raw path.

gates.B26_propBlockR_vs_drawnRadius: delta 0.000000 for every kind (bigrock 1.246, pebble 0.287, twig 0.214, mushroom 0.075)

stage5_group2_flora.abVsRawPath: 1 differing pixel out of 921,600, max channel delta 8.
stage5_group2_flora.sideMode: DoubleSide, never BackSide - FLORA_FS reads gl_FrontFacing and three implements BackSide as frontFace(CW)+cullFace(BACK), which inverts it (L8).

stage5_group3_decal_ghost.abVsRawPath: ghost with 27 instances: 0 differing pixels. decal never had instances in test - path shares the material construction, not separately exercised.
stage5_group3_decal_ghost.L5_secondOutput: DECAL_FS given a second output writing vec4(0.0) instead of a drawBuffers mask. Verified directly: attachment 1 is byte-identical with the pass on three vs raw (0 differing bytes of the whole RGBA8 buffer). Under addpre (ONE,ONE) dst+0=dst.
stage5_group3_decal_ghost.depthState: decal testTrue/writeFalse, ghost testFalse/writeFalse - the ghost must show through undug soil (B23).

stage5_group4_creatures.abVsRawPath: 2 differing pixels of 921,600 with all three uIsAnt groups populated (ants, queen, spider, 5 bestiary species, brood).

B16_broodSelector.nursery: tools/shots/s5_nursery.png - 2 eggs and 10 pupae, visibly distinct shapes, not identical beans

stage5_group4_creatures.uniformObjectPerMaterial: Four materials sharing one uniforms object would share one uIsAnt, which is exactly what separates an ant from a beetle from a brood stage. Keyed cache instead - stamping per group before each draw would appear to work and break the first time anything reordered them.
stage5_group4_creatures.instanceCountEqualsN: all 24 batches, including after a batch empties (drawThree zeroes it on the early return)

stage5_groups_5_6_7.liquids: droplets + puddles on three. LIQUID_FS already declares both outputs so no null-normal transform. 6 px vs a 2 px control.
stage5_groups_5_6_7.wet: ported with its multalpha blend, left DORMANT as the brief requires. Untested by construction - Game.pushWet returns immediately and there is no way to exercise it without enabling it.

billboards_HELD_ON_RAW.status: port written, verified NOT equivalent, left disabled behind R.useThreeBillboards

evidence.threeVsRaw: 144 px, max channel delta 381, same in both orders
evidence.perParticle: 49 particles on screen: 20 brighter through three, 0 brighter through raw - systematic and one-directional
evidence.worstPixel: 3x3 sprite present in the three frame, flat background in raw, 0.9 px from a live particle

ruledOut: GL state at the draw is byte-identical (blend ONE/ONE, eq ADD, depth test on, mask off, func LESS, cull off, CCW)
attachment 1 byte-identical, so the null-normal transform is not the cause
geometry, uniforms and instance arrays are the same objects

stage5_fallback_bug.finding: Props share the creature PROGRAM with the ants. Letting each group choose its path independently meant the prop raw fallback ran after the ants took the three branch, with no program bound - nothing had called R.useCreature.
stage5_fallback_bug.measured: 41,654 wrong pixels, max channel delta 363. Found by bisecting the material accessors one at a time against a control, not by looking at the frame.
stage5_fallback_bug.fix: one path decision for the whole creature-program group

ab_method_caveat.note: The double-render A/B (render, swap accessor, render, diff) has a noise floor. Two identical renders differ by 0-43 px depending on how much the particle system is emitting. Always measure a control - same path twice - in the same run, and compare group deltas against it rather than against zero.

stage6_sky.what: The sky fullscreen pass draws through three. Writes both MRT outputs, neither depth.

bug_found.symptom: GL error 1282 in drawTransparents, and sceneFB's depth buffer entirely 1.0 - nothing writing depth at all.
bug_found.cause: T3.Pass.render restores the default framebuffer when done, which is right for a post pass and wrong for a scene pass: every raw pass after beginScene assumes sceneFB is still bound and binds nothing itself. The whole opaque scene was drawing into the default framebuffer.
bug_found.whyItHid: The frame still looked broadly right. The tells were sceneFB depth staying empty, and colorOnly() calling drawBuffers([COLOR_ATTACHMENT0]) on the default framebuffer, which only accepts BACK or NONE.
bug_found.foundBy: wrapping every R.draw* entry point and checking glGetError plus the depth mask after each

stage6_heap.what: The sugar heap draws through three. Its interleaved 32-byte VBO maps onto THREE.InterleavedBuffer exactly, so m.vtx is handed over as-is rather than deinterleaved.
stage6_heap.abVsRawPath: 2 px against a 3 px control, with 960 units of sugar on screen - below the noise floor.
stage6_heap.note: T3B.drawObject deliberately does NOT call setRenderTarget: scene passes run inside a framebuffer the raw code bound, and taking ownership would restore the default framebuffer on the way out - the bug the sky pass hit.

stage6_glass_tubes.what: Glass panes and the connecting tubes on three - one program, per-draw uModel/uTint/uGlassCol.
stage6_glass_tubes.abVsRawPath: 0 differing pixels against a 0 px control. Attachment 1 byte-identical.
stage6_glass_tubes.depth: depthWrite off, depthFunc LESS. Panes sit +0.10 outside the soil box because flush panes z-fight with the raymarched surface; LEQUAL would make that pair last-drawn-wins (B24).

correction_resetState_unbinds_the_target.finding: three's resetState() unbinds the render target - it returns to the default framebuffer. So a resync makes the ambient binding the raw code left disappear, and any three draw that relied on it silently goes to the BACK buffer.
correction_resetState_unbinds_the_target.symptom: The glass drew into the back buffer, where the post chain then overwrote it. The frame looked almost right because glass is subtle. Attachment 1 was never written at all, so SSAO changed across the whole tank: 1,832,362 differing bytes, mean delta 104.
correction_resetState_unbinds_the_target.tell: DRAW_BUFFER0 read BACK instead of COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 at the draw call.
correction_resetState_unbinds_the_target.howToRead: Hook gl.drawElements and snapshot there. A post-hoc read after the draw shows three's end-of-render epilogue, not the state the draw used - it reported depthTest false when the draw had used true.
correction_resetState_unbinds_the_target.fix: T3B.drawObject binds sceneFB explicitly, renders, then hands the raw path its binding back.

stage6_statics.what: Room, table, table legs and vitrine frames on three - the only geometry carrying a real uModel.
stage6_statics.abVsRawPath: 1 differing pixel against a 1 px control.
stage6_statics.note: frustumCulled stays off even here: the object matrix lives in a uniform the shader applies itself, so three's bounds would be computed in the wrong space.

stage6_soil.what: The volumetric soil raymarch on three - gl_FragDepth, two sampler3Ds, the per-frame cull flip and uQuality.
stage6_soil.abVsRawPath: 2 differing pixels against a 2 px control.

gates.B10_L8_cullFlip: camera planted at the box centre: material.side flips to BackSide and the soil fills all 921,600 px. From outside, FrontSide, 644,892 px. The tank does not vanish.
gates.B8_viewportAfterDig: scoops 0 to 1, the very next frame lit across the full [0,0,1279,719] - not into a 96x60 corner.
gates.sampler3D: both bound through T3.extern3D - Data3DTexture for the TEXTURE_3D target with the GPU handle forced underneath, __version pinned so three never tries to upload over it.

probeGround.note: CPU-side measurement of ant y against farm.localTop. Proven independent of the render path: identical numbers through three and raw (worstAbove 0.026, worstBelow -4.819, 10 surface ants).
probeGround.worstBelow: -4.819 is an ant below ground, a pathing matter outside this stage and not caused by it - the identical raw-path reading is the proof.

stage6_soil.cullFlipTestTrap: avoidSoil pushes the camera back out of the box during rig.update, so a naive test reads side=FrontSide and proves nothing. The rig has to be stubbed for the duration of the render.

stage7_water_fullscreen.what: The water module's five targets and its four fullscreen passes - bilateral blur, thickness blur, normal rebuild, composite - on three. The two GL_POINTS impostor passes are still raw.
stage7_water_fullscreen.abVsRawPath: 12 differing pixels against a 6 px control, with the particles frozen so both paths draw identical water.

gates.halo: 738 pale px outside the true particle footprint, energy 4.00 - gate was <=1838 / <=5.95
gates.thicknessSweep@0.13: blue shift 0.269, darkening 0.155 - IDENTICAL through three and raw, so the 0.298/0.168 in the brief is a different pool, not a port regression
gates.inkOutline: 1911 px darkened - water receives an outline, which needs the composite's depth WRITE
gates.drainToZero: 3 ghost pixels with 0 particles gathered - no puddle left painted on the sand
gates.liveKnobs: WR.thickScale still takes effect at draw time (6868 px between 0.055 and 0.24) - B35 holds

notes.ivec2: three's setValueV2i calls gl.uniform2iv with whatever it is given and a Vector2 is not an array-like it accepts, so uDir/uSize are passed as plain arrays.
notes.compositeIsNotAPostPass: It writes gl_FragDepth, blends premultiplied into the scene target and writes both MRT outputs. T3.Pass defaults to no depth and no blend, all three of which are wrong here.
notes.pingPongEnds: depth blur ends in FB.depth, thickness blur ends in FB.thick. Swapping either leaves the normals rebuilt from an unsmoothed field.
notes.switch: WR.useThree gates the path so the two stay A/B-able from the console while both exist.

stage7_water_impostors.what: The two GL_POINTS impostor passes on three - THREE.Points over an InterleavedBuffer view of the SAME array WR.gather already fills, so there is one copy of the particle data.
stage7_water_impostors.abVsRawPath: 108 differing pixels of 1,024,000 against a 40 px control, particles frozen. 146,176 px of water drawn.

gates.inkOutline: 2721 px darkened - water receives an outline, which needs the composite's depth write
gates.liveKnobs: WR.thickScale still live at draw time: 142,270 px between 0.055 and 0.24
gates.drainToZero: 80 px of 1,024,000 with nothing gathered - no ghost puddle
gates.occlusion: grass and stones occlude the pool correctly in tools/shots/s7_water_full.png

halo_scene_dependence.finding: The gate numbers (1,838 px / 5.95 energy) are not scene-portable. On a 7,880 px footprint this build measures 738 px / 4.00, under the gate. On a 151,014 px footprint - a bigger pool, closer camera - the same build measures 15,615 px / 138.94.
halo_scene_dependence.whatMatters: three 15,615 px / 138.94 vs raw 16,309 px / 141.00 on the identical scene, three marginally better. The halo magnitude is a property of the scene, not of the port.
halo_scene_dependence.lesson: Quote a halo number with its footprint, or it means nothing.
